'''Joseph Anthony Ball''' (born 4 June 1947) is an American [[mathematician]] who is currently a professor emeritus <ref>{{Cite web | url=https://vtnews.vt.edu/articles/2016/09/science-josephballBofV.html | title=Joseph A. Ball of mathematics honored with emeritus status by Board of Visitors}}</ref> at the [[Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University]], often referred to as [[Virginia Tech]]. He is a 2019 fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] for contributions to [[operator theory]], [[analytic functions]], and service to the profession.<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list#b/ List of AMS Fellows]</ref>

He was awarded Bachelor of Science from [[Georgetown University]] in 1969. He obtained his Master of Science in 1970 and Doctor of Philosophy in 1973 both from the [[University of Virginia]], [[Charlottesville]]. The title of his doctoral dissertation is "Unitary Perturbations of
Contractions", supervised by Marvin Rosenblum.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=15632 | title=Marvin Rosenblum – the Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> According to current [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]] database, Ball has 12 students and 18 descendants.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=15797 | title=Joseph Ball – the Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref>
